_comment: GitHub configuration this repository cannot express in code, kept here so the intent is
versioned, reviewable and reproducible instead of living in one person's browser tab.
Apply it with scripts/apply-repo-config.sh. Edit this file, never the web UI.
Until now the `push dev` ruleset had no required status checks at all, so every CI job was
decorative at the moment of merging: red, and mergeable anyway. These are the checks that
report on every pull request to dev, which is the condition for being required at all.
_bypassComment: A bypass exception on this ruleset bypasses all of it, required checks included, so on the dev
boundary these make merging red a deliberate act rather than the default. That is the intent:
one person works on Jump today and must not be blocked by the absence of a second reviewer.
bypass_actors is only returned to an admin, so apply-repo-config.sh round-trips whatever the
GET returned and never defaults it to an empty list, which would revoke the exception.
requiredStatusChecks._strictComment: false: do not force the branch to be up to date with dev before merging. With merge commits and mostly solo work, that only adds churn.
_deterministicComment: Every check above answers the same way for the same diff: it reads this repository and nothing
else. That is the condition for blocking a merge, because a required check that can turn red on
its own turns every open pull request red on its own, and no change to the branch clears it.
The same argument is why SAST pins its rulesets instead of using `--config auto`.

excluded.DAST (OWASP ZAP): Guarded by `if: schedule || push to main`, so it never reports on a pull request. Requiring it would leave every merge waiting for a status that never arrives.
excluded.Docker Image Scan: Builds the whole image. Useful, but a merge into dev should not wait on it.
excluded.Dependency Audit: Not deterministic: osv-scanner resolves advisories against the live OSV database, so an advisory published tonight fails every pull request tomorrow with no diff change and no per-branch fix. It still runs on every pull request and is still red when it matters, and the weekly `schedule` run is what catches a new advisory against a branch nobody touched. Blocking the merge on it would repeat the Docker Hub outage that took this repository's image scan down.
